To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of Bax is increased in cancerous prostatic epithelium, and in the highest grades of carcinoma.

the expression of Bax, Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL in normal epithelum of cancerous prostatse was increased in comparison to controls and was associated with the presence of PIN, Gleason grade 3–5 carcinomas, perineural invasion, and capsular invasion.
the expression of Bax was significantly higher in cancerous prostatic epithelium than in normal prostatic epithelum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of prostate cancer and the role of apoptosis in this process.
the role of Bax and/or Bcl-2 expression in the development of prostate carcinoma.
the molecular mechanisms of prostate carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bax and BCl-2 expression is not a reliable marker for the detection of prostate cancer.

apoptosis is disturbed in cancerous prostate and the disturbance is most prominent in high-grade carcinomas and in foci with capsular perineuronal invasion, suggesting that the apoptotic control is involved in local progression of prostate carcinomas.
Bax and BcL-2 are focall overexpressed in cancerous prostate and in PIN foci, but not in benign hyperplasia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Bax and BCL-2 are focallly expressed in the normal epithelia of cancerous prostatas.
the apoptotic control is generally disturbed in the prostate and that it seems to be involved in the local progression of prostate carcinomas.
Bax and BCl-2 may be useful in the early detection of prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of Bax, a proapoptotic protein, is higher in the normal epithelia of cancerous prostatic glands, and that the expression of this protein in cancerous prostatic tissues is highest in foci of capsular perineuronal invasion.
Bcl-2 and Bax can be used as indirect markers of apoptosis in prostate cancer.
Bax and BCL2 are overexpressed in normal epithelum of cancerous prostatas, and this overexpression is associated with the Gleason grade of the cancer.
